name: line_quality

state.task: Judge the OCR text of `line`, one line recognised from a scanned page of an archaeological report or related material from a Czech archive (1920–2020). `before` and `after` are its neighbours on the page.

scope: text quality only: what the OCR text of the line shows. The page's orientation and script are its form, read from the image by atrium-page-classification (B4 orientation, B3 elements); f_inverted_letters and f_script_misread name patterns in the text and assert nothing about the page
source: #10 plan, Phase B (2026-11-08; v2 2026-11-09, the page-level factors reworded as text symptoms): the factors mirror the rule detectors of docs/reference/categorization_rules.md

f_symbols.instructions: Does `line` contain stray symbols or punctuation that are not part of any word (e.g. ¦ § ~ ^ |)?

f_digits.instructions: Are digits mixed into words, or is `line` mostly numbers and fragments where words are expected?

f_repeated.instructions: Does `line` contain runs of one repeated character or letter pair (e.g. `iiii`, `ididid`)?

f_few_vowels.instructions: Does `line` contain letter strings with too few vowels to be words (e.g. `HRPSTK`, `vfrbn`)?

f_gibberish.instructions: Does `line` contain letter strings that are not words in any language?

f_case.instructions: Are capital letters out of place inside words (e.g. `dalSÍ`)?

f_misread_letters.instructions: Are some letters misread in otherwise recognisable words (e.g. `fraament okraie` for `fragment okraje`, or lost diacritics)?

f_split_merged.instructions: Are words broken into fragments, or run together without spaces?

f_inverted_letters.instructions: Is `line` made of letter shapes and combinations that no word uses (many w, x, q, or symbols in place of letters), as OCR gives for text it read upside down or mirrored?

f_script_misread.instructions: Are nearly all letters of `line` wrong while its word lengths and spacing still look like writing, as OCR gives when it reads handwriting as print?

f_foreign.instructions: Is `line` written in a language other than Czech or Slovak?

criteria: mostly garbage: a few words can be recognised
damaged: readable with effort, many errors
minor errors: readable, with a few wrong letters or symbols
quality.instructions: How good is the OCR text of `line`?
